subject: jumping spider
title: A Spider With a Sesame-Seed Brain Plans Its Attack Out of Sight

scenes.text: This spider walks away from its prey on purpose.
Some jumping spiders hunt only other spiders. Scientists starved them for a week.
Then they gave them a puzzle: food on a tower, two paths, and only one leading there.
To take the right path, the spider has to lose sight of its prey for the whole trip.
Across about fifteen species, they picked the correct path far more often than chance.
They plan the route first, and their brain is the size of a sesame seed.

description:
Spartaeine jumping spiders, the group that includes Portia, hunt other spiders. In a 2016 study, spiders of about 15 species were shown prey on a tower reachable by only one of two walkways; to get there they had to lose sight of the prey along the way, and they chose the right walkway significantly more often than the wrong one.
Researchers say the planning seems unlearned and widespread in the group, in a brain about the size of a sesame seed.
What's the smartest small animal you know?
first_comment: A brain the size of a sesame seed, and it plans a route. What's the smartest thing you've seen a spider do?
